Is SailfishOS a good alternative?

No. At least not for personal use. SailfishOS is not in a shape where normal regular consumers can use it at this time. It's currently targetting corporations and governments for work use with security at its heart. SailfishOS is developed in Finland and is currently used by e.g. Russian government because it is the only serious independent non-American mobile OS on the market.

SFOS has a very sexy and exotic but intuitive gesture based UI (which was borrowed from N9's Meego-Harmattan) but also comes with a lot of issues relating to available software and services. I have several Sailfish devices and so far the best has been Jolla 1 where everything just works (esp. drivers for camera).

I currently use SailfishX which is basically a distribution of SFOS for Sony Xperia X and XA2 devices. I have Xperia X which I think Jolla has probably quietly and unofficially abandoned due to lack of driver and feature updates they promised to deliver but thus far have not done that. For example SailfishX for XperiaX's camera has several bad bugs e.g. relating to autofocus, NFC support practically isn't there, radio is nowhere to be seen, Android support lagging behind (4.4 instead of 8.1) etc.

More general issues with SFOS are that due to hardened web browser based on Mozilla Gecko engine, the web browser is incapable for example showing Twitter.com and some other popular web sites currently. The secure memory restrictions cause sometimes active programs on background (for example media player playing music which you browse web and have email client open) to randomly shutdown suddenly without a warning.

There are minor UI bugs some of which are related to the tablet support the OS is capable of providing. SFOS 3.0 release broke some of the touch gestures like "swipe from outside of top edge towards centre to close app" and now it it's "swipe from 45" degree angle from top corners towards centre to close app" which sucks ass because it's difficult to pull with one hand in move. The reason they did that was to have a Android style control centre showing up from the top swipe. Which is kind of useful but it takes away more than it brings on the table since notifications are located in their own carousel page in main view.

All software is basically written by SFOS community without a pay since the Jolla Store doesn't support paid apps (which was promised in 2013 but never delivered). There are no official native Twitter, Reddit, Minds, WhatsApp, Youtube, Facebook, Gab, Spotify, Voat, Instagram, Imgur, etc. clients for SFOS. You have to use community made clients or make your own. Sailfish does provide some Twitter and Facebook integration options but in a very limited manner. If you want to know more about issues with it, head to https://together.jolla.com/questions/ for more up to date situation on everything.

But yeah, I wouldn't recommend SFOS right now for anyone except the tinfoil hat people, hackers (as in tinkerers) who want to do their own thing and computer programmers seeking an alternative platform to play with on their free time. I've come to SFOS from Maemo/Meego as a programmer and tinkerer and I've kind of been stuck in that ecosystem ever since. I'd like to love SFOS but it's not really loving me back. At least Jolla is actively developing SFOS and maybe in future it might turn out to be a good alternative. However the fact of life is that right now it is not suitable for normie use.
